facts: Early computer memory could store data on the surface of a spinning magnetic drum.
William Grey Walter built small wheeled robots that responded to light.
Walter's robot Elsie sought moderate light while avoiding very bright light and darkness.
Isaac Asimov's I, Robot is a collection of nine stories, not a single novel.
Asimov's fictional robots followed rules intended to protect humans.
Britain's Pilot ACE computer was based on ideas from Alan Turing.
Plans for the Simon computer were published in a hobbyist electronics magazine.
The Simon computer was designed to fit into roughly the space of a large box.
Russell Kirsch made an early scanned digital image using the SEAC computer in 1957.
The SWAC computer helped researchers discover previously unknown prime numbers.
COBOL's name expands to Common Business-Oriented Language.
COBOL was designed to make business programs relatively easy to read.
COBOL's designers wanted programs to work on different manufacturers' computers.
A worried COBOL committee member had a mock tombstone made for the language in 1960.
The early video game Spacewar! was developed on a PDP-1 computer.
MIT programmers also made music with the PDP-1.
The PDP-1 used paper tape to get information into and out of the computer.
An early Japanese NEAC computer could handle both alphabetic and kana characters.
A NEAC computer operated an early real-time railway reservation system in Japan.
Tony Hoare developed Quicksort while working on machine translation in Moscow.
Some early cash machines read specially treated, slightly radioactive paper vouchers.
Barclays introduced an early public cash machine in Britain in 1967.
Automated banking involved behind-the-scenes cheque processing before cash machines became common.
The unusual characters printed along the bottom of cheques help machines process them.
The Pascal programming language was named after Blaise Pascal.
Niklaus Wirth designed Pascal partly as a language for teaching programming.
Pascal was intended for scientific and business work, not just classroom exercises.
Gene Amdahl left IBM and founded a company to compete with its mainframes.
Amdahl's mainframes could run software written for IBM systems.
IBM's move from magnetic cores to semiconductor memory reduced the space needed to store data.
William Shatner appeared in advertisements for Commodore's VIC-20 computer.
The Commodore VIC-20 became the first computer to sell more than a million units.
The VIC-20 was designed as a cheaper alternative to Commodore's PET computer.
Before creating the Web, Tim Berners-Lee built a hypertext system called Enquire.
Berners-Lee named Enquire after a Victorian reference book he enjoyed as a child.
Enquire was used for managing projects at CERN.
Enquire explored links that computers, as well as people, could interpret.
Seagate's early ST506 hard drive stored just five megabytes.
The ST506 was designed to fit into the space used by a floppy drive.
Hard drives store information magnetically on coated, rotating platters.
Some rewritable discs combined lasers and magnets to store information.
Magneto-optical discs heated tiny areas with a laser before changing their magnetic state.
Magneto-optical discs came in protective cartridges.
Some magneto-optical discs could be rewritten around a million times.
Intel's Touchstone Delta supercomputer used 512 processors working together.
Researchers used Touchstone Delta to process satellite pictures.
Touchstone Delta also helped researchers simulate molecules.
Windows 3.0 could still run older DOS programs.
Windows 3.0 helped popularise graphical applications on personal computers.
New magnetic reading heads helped hard drives pack data more densely in 1990.
Characters in The Sims speak an invented language called Simlish.
The Sims lets players manage everyday lives rather than complete one fixed final mission.
The Sims was led by designer Will Wright, who had previously created SimCity.
The Sims let players customise their characters and homes.
An early Sharp camera phone took pictures at only 0.11 megapixels.
Sharp's J-SH04 phone could share photographs wirelessly.
Honda's ASIMO robot could climb stairs.
ASIMO used a camera in its head to recognise faces and gestures.
ASIMO could respond to voice commands through built-in microphones.
The PlayStation 2 helped popularise DVDs because it played films as well as games.
